- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overreacts to volatility.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting mean reversion is not captured well.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in downward trends — model reacts too slowly.
- Model often fails to account for sudden drops after recent highs — underestimates risk of sharp reversals.
- In low-volatility periods, model overestimates mean price, ignoring recent downward drift.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust to new information quickly, especially when true price deviates from forecast mid-horizon.
